newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's League promises budget filibustering.
newsitem.headline: Italy's League promises budget filibustering.

text.p: The federalist Northern League said it would use filibustering tactics to slow passage of the 1997 Italian budget through parliament, the party leader in the Lower House of parliament said on Thursday.
"Ours will be an obstructionist opposition within the bounds of the law," Domenico Comino said in a radio interview.

He added that the League, which last month declared "independence" for the north of Italy, would organise a series of demonstrations against the government's 62.5 trillion lire deficit cutting budget.
The package, which includes a one-off "Euro-tax", will be formally unveiled to parliament on Thursday. It has to be approved by both houses of parliament before the end of 1996.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi used confidence motions to side-step dogged League filibustering when a government mini-budget passed before parliament earlier this year. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
